newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares inch higher, but outlook cloudy.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares inch higher, but outlook cloudy.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose on Friday, but traders said shares may track sideways over the short term as the composition of the next government remains a big question mark.
"Foreigners are still waiting and watching who will be in the next government," Karmen Cerar, a trader of brokerage Poteza said.
The final unofficial election results show that the ruling centre-left Liberal Democrats would get 25 seats in the new 90 seat parliament.
Liberal Democrats may therefore have to hand over power to the rightist "Spring" alliance consisting of the People's Party, Social Democrats and Christian Democrats.
Analysts said that shares prices may fall if the "Spring Parties" manage to form a government because of their protective stand towards Slovenia joining the European Union.
The SBI index rose 1.74 points or 0.16 percent to 1,175.4. Overall six shares rose, seven fell and one was unchanged, while 10 were untraded.
Turnover rose to 193.6 million tolars from 177.4 million.
Traders said turnover would likely remain low until the next government is formed.
Bank SKB was the day's most active share, falling 2.15 percent to 43,180 tolars on volume of 3,172 shares for total turnover of 140.9 million tolars.
"SKB fell today mostly in a technical reaction to yesterday's high jump," one trader said. On Thursday, shareholders approved the bank's decision to list on foreign bourses.
Bank Dolenjska banka was the biggest gainer, rising 3.51 percent to 11,800 tolars on volume of 102 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 5.62 percent to 25,000 tolars on volume of 46 shares.
